title: The Recursive Fencing Where Lines Study Each Other

features.name: the boundary line
features.desc-on-touch: A fence studies its own edges. Where does it end and where does it know itself to begin?

features.name: lattice watching lattice
features.desc-on-touch: Two fencelines cross and both pause to read what the other one is saying. Their geometry is identical. Their observations differ.

features.name: the center that moved
features.desc-on-touch: A boundary marked a center once. Now it is a center studying what used to mark it. The roles keep swapping.

features.name: the recursive gaze
features.desc-on-touch: Every fence here is looking at every other fence. The looking is the fencing. The study is the boundary.

features.name: property made conscious
features.desc-on-touch: Land divided by lines that know they divide. The fences grew aware they were creating the properties they supposedly separated.

inscription: every boundary is a center from the other side; here the fences learned to stand at both edges at once

file.name: Cadastral_Recursive_Survey_1947.txt
file.note: original property map; annotations spiral inward with observations about which side of each line the observer stood
